newsitem.title: USA: Ultrak sees Q1 primary shr $0.16-$0.18.
newsitem.headline: Ultrak sees Q1 primary shr $0.16-$0.18.

text.p: Ultrak Inc said it expected first quarter primary earnings from operations of $0.16 to $0.18 per share, not including a $0.03 per share non-recurring expense associated with the termination of its merger with Checkpoint Systems Inc.

The First Call consensus earnings estimate for the first quarter was $0.21 per share versus $0.16 per share earned in the year-ago quarter. On February 19, the company said it was "comfortable" with such estimates.
Ultrak said it expected first quarter revenues of about $42 million versus $30 million in the same quarter last year.
Securities and surveillance product provider Checkpoint Systems said on Thursday its agreement to merge with Ultrak was terminated by mutual consent.
It said the main reason for the termination was perceived "channel conflict" with Ultrak's distribution network.
Under terms of the pact, each Ultrak share would have been exchanged for 1.15 Checkpoint shares. Wall Street arbitrage traders said then the deal was valued at about $397 million.

Ultrak, which designs, makes, markets and services closed-circuit television and related products for use in security and surveillance, said its sales picked up in February and March but not as much as expected.
An attempt to unify its domestic sales force might have contributed to a temporary sales slowdown, Ultrak said.
In January, the company united its four domestic professional security and surveillance sales forces into a single selling group geared to the distributor and dealer channel, Ultrak said.
European operations were hurt by unfavorable exchange rates, the company said.
First quarter sales to the casino market were below plan but were seen improving in the future, it said.
Revenues were also hurt by the timing of certain orders in the do-it-yourself consumer market, Ultrak said.

"Despite a slow start this year, we are more confident than ever about the path we have chosen, which is to develop and acquire the most comprehensive family of world-class CCTV and related products and technologies and to build worldwide marketing capabilities to maximize market coverage and speed to market," Chief Executive George Broady said.
